title: The Commission of Inquiry led by General Sir Veerasamy Ringadoo uncovered a significant drug trafficking network in Mauritius, involving high-profile individuals such as MPs, police officers, and businessmen. The inquiry received extensive media coverage, revealing that many of these individuals were deeply entrenched in the drug trade, often using their positions to evade scrutiny. Notably, former Chief Whip Harish Boodhoo emerged as a whistleblower, exposing corrupt MPs, while Harris Mungroosingh, head of the Anti Drug and Smuggling Unit, was implicated as a traitor for tipping off drug barons. The report recommended stricter laws to combat drug trafficking, including measures to enhance financial transparency and increase penalties for drug-related offenses. Prime Minister Aneerood Jugnauth expressed satisfaction with the findings, indicating a commitment to addressing the drug issue in Mauritius.
